extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys and USPTO disciplinary officials (OED), and attorneys facing USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order in an Office discipline proceeding describing stipulated facts, legal conclusions, findings of state-court ethical violations, the ground for exclusion from practice before the USPTO, required post-exclusion duties, publication/notice obligations, and reinstatement conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement meeting 37 C.F.R. §10.133(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent submitted a proposed settlement agreement that sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to resolve voluntarily the disciplinary proceeding and obviate an administrative hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. §10.133(g) and resolve disciplinary action arising from evidence previously submitted to the USPTO's Committee on Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for exclusion: disbarment on ethical grounds (37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's conduct violated 37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(5) because Respondent was disbarred from practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by the Supreme Court of Arizona.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being disbarred on ethical grounds by a state's highest court is a basis for exclusion from practice before the USPTO under the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of exclusion from practice before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from practicing patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office commencing with the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion is the primary sanction imposed by this Final Order; it prohibits all authorized practice before the USPTO as specified in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice in the Official Gazette stating Respondent's exclusion, registration number, and the statutory and regulatory basis for the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice text should identify the respondent, registration number, the regulatory violation (37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(5)), and note the statutory authority (35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §§10.133(g) and 10.159).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to interested offices and authorities (37 C.F.R. §10.159)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the Final Order to appropriate employees of the Office; interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; appropriate authorities of any State in which the practitioner is known to be a member of the bar; and any appropriate bar association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad institutional notice is required so other agencies and bar authorities are informed of the practitioner's exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to bars and clients within 30 days (37 C.F.R. §10.158(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of entry of the Final Order, Respondent must notify in separate written communications all bars of which Respondent is a member and all clients for whom he is handling matters before the Office, if any, of the exclusion and file a copy of each written communication with the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications must be separate written communications and copies must be filed with OED to document compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender of clients' active USPTO case files (37 C.F.R. §10.158(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the date of the Final Order, Respondent must surrender each client's active USPTO case file(s), if any, to each client or to another practitioner designated by each client and file proof thereof with the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of surrender must be filed with the OED Director to show compliance with client-file transfer obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of unearned funds and client property (37 C.F.R. §§10.158(b)(8) and 10.160(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the date of the Final Order, Respondent must return to any client having immediate or prospective business before the Office any unearned legal funds, including any unearned retainer fee, and any securities and property of the client; and file proof with the OED Director no later than the date Respondent files his petition for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returning client funds and property promptly and filing proof are prerequisites for later reinstatement proceedings and protect client interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspend and forward communications; no legal action or advice during exclusion (37 C.F.R. §§10.158(a),(b)(2),(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period of exclusion, Respondent must suspend all communication relating to a client matter, immediately forward to the client or the practitioner's designee all communications relating to a client matter that are addressed to or received by Respondent, and take no legal action, enter any appearance, or provide any legal advice concerning any matter that is the subject of the client communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must cease all client-representation activities before the Office and promptly forward incoming communications to preserve client rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove advertising/media indicating authorization to practice; file affidavit (37 C.F.R. §§10.158(b)(4) and (b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must promptly take steps to remove from telephone books, legal directories, signs, letterheads, and other media all advertisements, statements, representations, and other indications that would reasonably suggest authorization to practice before the Office and file an affidavit describing the precise nature of the steps taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must remove all materials that could mislead the public about authorization to practice and must document the remedial steps in an affidavit filed with the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on holding out, advertising, or rendering legal services for USPTO matters during exclusion (37 C.F.R. §§10.158(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period of exclusion, Respondent shall not engage in unauthorized practice before the Office; not hold himself out as authorized to practice before the Office; not advertise availability or ability to perform legal services for any person having immediate, prospective, or pending business before the Office; and not render legal advice or services to any person having immediate, prospective, or pending business before the Office as to that business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prohibitions comprehensively bar any representation, advertising, or advisory activities for matters that could be before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and compliance if acting as paralegal or assisting another practitioner (37 C.F.R. §§10.158(c) and (d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent acts as a paralegal or aids or endeavors to assist a practitioner in the other practitioner's practice of law before the Office during exclusion, Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. §§10.158(c) and (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even ancillary or support roles relating to USPTO practice are regulated and require compliance with the specified subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on being named as inventor or co-inventor on clients' patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not hereinafter be named as an inventor or co-inventor in any patent application based on a client's invention unless (a) the client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing by the client, and (b) Respondent otherwise fully complies with all applicable rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the excluded practitioner as inventor requires documented client informed consent and full compliance with professional responsibility rules to avoid conflicts or misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement waiting period and requirements (37 C.F.R. §10.160)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may not be considered for reinstatement until five years after the effective date of his exclusion; thereafter, he may apply for reinstatement by filing a petition and an affidavit showing compliance with specified conditions including compliance with 37 C.F.R. §§10.158 and 10.150.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A five-year minimum wait applies; reinstatement requires documentary proof of compliance with prior-order obligations and adherence to the USPTO professional responsibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions applied at reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: If and when Respondent applies for reinstatement, the OED Director conclusively presumes, for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the stipulated facts and the hearing officer's findings of fact are true, and (ii) Respondent could not have successfully defended himself against the legal conclusions stemming from those facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stipulated and previously-adjudicated factual findings are treated as conclusively true in the reinstatement evaluation, creating a heavy evidentiary burden for the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each party bears own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No costs awarded between the parties as part of this settlement; each pays its own expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.4 — Failure to disclose information (Arizona Rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated Ethical Rule (ER) 1.4 by failing to disclose information to TASER that Respondent knew could impact the representation of TASER's business interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to disclose material information to a client that could affect representation is a sanctionable ethical violation under the cited state rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.6 — Misappropriation/use of client information
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 1.6 by misappropriating information learned during the course of the representation of TASER and using such information to harm TASER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using confidential client information to the client's detriment constitutes a breach of duties of confidentiality and loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.7(a)(2) — Conflict of interest: representation materially limited by self-interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 1.7(a)(2) by continuing to represent TASER at a time when the representation of TASER was materially limited by Respondent's self-interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing representation despite material limitations from a lawyer's personal interests is improper conflict management.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.8(a) and ER 8.4(a) — Improper business transaction/adverse ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 1.8(a) and 8.4(a) by attempting to enter into a business transaction with TASER or by attempting to wrongly acquire an ownership interest adverse to TASER without TASER's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entering business transactions with a client or acquiring adverse ownership without informed consent is prohibited and may form the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.8(a) — Acquiring client stock without complying with ER 1.8(a)(2) or (3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 1.8(a) by acquiring TASER stock without complying with the provisions of ER 1.8(a)(2) or (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisitions of client property or securities require compliance with the specific subparagraphs governing such transactions (disclosure, fairness, written consent, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.8(b) — Using information to client's disadvantage without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 1.8(b) by using information relating to the representation of TASER to the disadvantage of TASER without TASER's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using client-related information in a way that harms the client without consent breaches fiduciary duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.90) — Using representation information to provoke interference (as stated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 1.90) by using information relating to the representation of TASER by provoking an interference with a patent application that Respondent had previously filed with the Office on behalf of TASER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provoking interferences or otherwise manipulating patent proceedings using client information can constitute professional misconduct (note: ER citation is quoted as in the Order).

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.13(b) — Failure to advise client about suspected theft and declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 1.13(b) by failing to advise TASER that Respondent believed one of TASER's employees had stolen the technology giving rise to certain technology and had signed a declaration under oath claiming sole inventorship of the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lawyer must advise an organizational client of information reasonably necessary to enable the client to protect its interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 1.16(a)(1) — Failure to withdraw when representation violates rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 1.16(a)(1) by failing to withdraw from representing TASER in connection with the patent prosecution of certain technology as the representation violated the Arizona Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When continued representation would violate ethical rules, the lawyer must withdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 3.3(a), ER 3.4(b), and ER 8.4(c) — Filing and failing to correct false declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 3.3(a), 3.4(b), and ER 8.4(c) by filing declarations Respondent believed to be factually false with the Office and then failing to correct the false declarations Respondent filed on behalf of TASER employees in support of the patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting false statements or declarations to tribunals or failing to correct known falsehoods is a serious ethical violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 5.4(a) — Sharing legal fees with a non-lawyer
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 5.4(a) by sharing legal fees with a non-lawyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee-sharing with non-lawyers is typically prohibited under professional conduct rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER 8.4(d) — Engaging in wrongful conduct during and after representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated ER 8.4(d) by engaging in conduct during and after this representation (as stated in the Order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ER 8.4(d) captures conduct that seriously interferes with the administration of justice or involves dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or reckless or intentional misrepresentation; the Order applies that rule to Respondent's conduct.
